## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_app_state({ include_schema: true, include_canvas_design: true, include_scripts_and_shaders: false }) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. All three flags are required. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_app_state, get_guidelines, execute, get_screenshot, export_nodes, export_html.
Also: browser.

{"body":"Part of #649

`comp:desktop` · **M** · `crates/fuse/src/adapters/windows.rs`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

**Problem.** Windows has no mount path, and the `Cargo Check & Test (Windows)` job has no adapter to check — it is the authoritative leg for this adapter by design.

**Scope.** A WinFsp adapter with case-insensitive lookup presentation (collision behaviour stays the engine's one strict comparator), the `VfsError` → NTSTATUS mapping, and the WinFsp notify API on the invalidation callback; pinned WinFsp MSI provisioning in the Windows CI leg.

`SpillArea::open(dir, entropy)` must be constructed from the **production `getrandom` seam** — spill files use counter nonces under a per-file random key, so a seeded or test entropy source in production is a nonce-reuse break, not a weakening.

**AC sketch.** The NTSTATUS mapping is table-tested; case-insensitive lookup finds an as-entered name while the comparator still decides collisions; the spill's close-before-unlink ordering is exercised on this leg (it is exercised nowhere else).

# WinFsp License Summary

## Base License
WinFsp is licensed under GPLv3. The full GPLv3 terms apply, requiring that any distributed modifications include source code and remain under GPL.

## FLOSS Exception
Bill Zissimopoulos grants a special exception permitting FLOSS projects to:

1. **Link against WinFsp DLLs** without triggering GPL obligations for the linking software
2. **Distribute unmodified WinFsp installer binaries** without GPL requirements

### Qualifying Licenses
Projects must be distributed under licenses satisfying either:
- "the Free Software Definition Version 1.141" or
- "the Open Source Definition Version 1.9"

### Conditions for Exception
The software using this exception must:
1. Include the copyright notice: "WinFsp - Windows File System Proxy, Copyright (C) Bill Zissimopoulos" plus a link to the WinFsp repository in UI and documentation
2. Remain free/open source only—"not linked or distributed with proprietary (non-FLOSS) software"

## Commercial Licensing
Projects that cannot meet these conditions (particularly those mixing FLOSS with proprietary components) require commercial licensing from Bill Zissimopoulos (billziss at navimatics.com).

## 1. `apps/api` structure and auth routes

Monorepo: pnpm workspaces (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`), API package is `@cipherbox/api`, `"type": "commonjs"`, NestJS 11. Auth module: `<root>/apps/api/src/auth/auth.module.ts`

- `JwtModule.registerAsync({ useFactory: buildJwtOptions })`

### `AuthController` — `<root>/apps/api/src/auth/auth.controller.ts`, `@Controller('auth')`, `@ApiTags('Auth')`

| Route | Method/status | Guard | Throttle surface | Response DTO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/challenge` | `@HttpCode(200)` | none | `auth` | `ChallengeResponseDto` |
| `POST /auth/login` | 200 | none | `auth` | `TokenResponseDto` |
| `POST /auth/siwe/challenge` | 200 | none | `auth` | `SiweChallengeResponseDto` |
| `POST /auth/siwe/login` | 200 | none | `auth` | `TokenResponseDto` |
| `POST /auth/siwe/link` | 201 (default) | `JwtAuthGuard` | `auth` | `LogoutResponseDto` |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | 200 | none | `refresh` | `TokenResponseDto` |
| `POST /auth/logout` | 200 | `JwtAuthGuard` | global | `LogoutResponseDto` |
| `POST /auth/test-login` | 200 | none | `auth` | `TestLoginResponseDto` |

Handler signatures:
- `challenge(@Body() body: ChallengeRequestDto): ChallengeResponseDto`
- `login(@Body() body: LoginRequestDto, @Res({passthrough:true}) response: Response): Promise<TokenResponseDto>`
- `refresh(@Body() body: RefreshRequestDto, @Req() request: Request, @Res({passthrough:true}) response: Response): Promise<TokenResponseDto>`

`IdentityController` — same `@Controller('auth')` prefix, `@ApiTags('Identity')`, at `<root>/apps/api/src/auth/identity.controller.ts`: `GET /auth/.well-known/jwks.json`, `POST /auth/identity/google`, `/auth/identity/email/send-code`, `/auth/identity/email/verify-code`, `/auth/identity/wallet`. ### Exact login/refresh response shape

`<root>/apps/api/src/auth/dto/auth.dto.ts`:

```ts
export class TokenResponseDto {
  @ApiProperty({ description: 'Short-lived access JWT' })
  accessToken!: string;
  @ApiProperty({ description: 'Rotating refresh token (...)' })
  refreshToken!: string;
  @ApiPropertyOptional({ description: 'True when this login created the account implicitly' })

```

- `POST /auth/login` returns `{ ...pair, isNewUser }` → `{ accessToken, refreshToken, isNewUser }`.
- `POST /auth/refresh` returns `pair` only → `{ accessToken, refreshToken }` (no `isNewUser`).
- `TestLoginResponseDto extends TokenResponseDto` adds `publicKey`, `privateKey`.

## 2. Token minting, TTLs, rotation

`<root>/apps/api/src/auth/services/token.service.ts` — `TokenService`, constructor injects `JwtService, Clock, Entropy, ConfigService, @InjectRepository(RefreshToken) Repository<RefreshToken>`.

Public surface (these are the exact seams to hook a new per-session token into):
- `createTokenPair(userId: string, publicKey: string): Promise<TokenPair>` — signs access JWT + `mintRefreshToken(userId, this.entropy.randomUuid())` (new family).
- `createScopedToken(userId: string, scope: TokenScope): Promise<ScopedToken>` — capability token, no refresh family; returns `{ accessToken, expiresIn }`.
- `rotate(rawToken: string, publicKeyByUserId: (userId: string) => Promise<string>): Promise<TokenPair>`
- `revokeAllForUser(userId: string): Promise<void>` — hard delete by `userId`.
- `get refreshTokenTtlMs(): number`
- private `signAccessToken(userId, publicKey)` → `jwtService.signAsync({ sub: userId, publicKey })`; private `mintRefreshToken(userId, familyId)`; private `hashToken(rawToken)` → `createHash('sha256').update(rawToken).digest('hex')`.

Interfaces: `export interface TokenPair { accessToken: string; refreshToken: string }`, `export interface ScopedToken { accessToken: string; expiresIn: number }`.

JWT signing config: `buildJwtOptions(configService: ConfigService)` exported from `<root>/apps/api/src/auth/auth.module.ts` — HS256 via `secret`; throws `JWT_SECRET is required when NODE_ENV is '<env>'` outside `development`/`test`; dev fallback secret `'cipherbox-dev-jwt-secret'`; `signOptions: { expiresIn: accessTtlSeconds }`.

TTLs / env vars (all read via `ConfigService`, none documented in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` — that file is explicitly marked a v1 doc):
- `ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` — default `900` (auth.module.ts). **This is the TTL your accelerator token must mirror.**
- `REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_DAYS` — default `7` → `refreshTtlMs` (token.service.ts).
- `SCOPED_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS` — default 600, hard ceiling 3600, via `positiveIntConfig` (`<root>/apps/api/src/common/config-int.ts`).
- `JWT_SECRET`, `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, `DB_ADVISORY_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 3000), `THROTTLE_TTL_MS`, `THROTTLE_LIMIT`, `THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT`.
- Env template: `<root>/apps/api/.env.example` (documents `JWT_SECRET`, `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`, DB, `KUBO_API_URL`, `ROUTING_V1_URL`, `IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `MAIL_PROVIDER`). It does **not** list the TTL vars.

Rotation mechanics in `rotate()` (order matters):
1. `findOne({ where: { tokenHash } })`; miss → 401 `'Invalid refresh token'`.
2. `usedAt !== null` → **reuse**: `delete({ familyId })`, `logger.warn`, 401.
3. expired → `delete({ familyId })`, 401 `'Refresh token expired'`.
4. Atomic single-use claim: `update({ id, usedAt: IsNull() }, { usedAt: now })`; `!claim.affected` → delete family, 401.
5. Opportunistic sweep: `delete({ userId, expiresAt: LessThan(now) })`.
6. `publicKey = await publicKeyByUserId(userId)`; sign new access token; `mintRefreshToken(userId, existing.familyId)` (same family).

Persistence: yes — table `refresh_tokens`, entity `RefreshToken` at `<root>/apps/api/src/auth/entities/refresh-token.entity.ts`. Raw token never stored; only `sha256` hex. Mint sites for a token pair are exactly two: `AuthService.identityLogin` / `AuthService.siweLogin` (`<root>/apps/api/src/auth/services/auth.service.ts`) and `TestAuthService.testLogin` (`<root>/apps/api/src/auth/services/test-auth.service.ts`), plus `AuthService.refresh(rawRefreshToken)` which delegates to `tokenService.rotate` with a `publicKeyByUserId` closure over the `users` repo.

`Clock` and `Entropy` are injected abstract classes (`<root>/apps/api/src/common/clock.ts`, `<root>/apps/api/src/common/entropy.ts`), provided globally by `RuntimeModule` (`<root>/apps/api/src/common/runtime.module.ts`). **House rule (AGENTS.md code-gen rule 4): never call `Date.now()`/`randomBytes` directly — use these.** `Entropy.randomUuid()` is available for a pseudonym id.

ORM: **TypeORM 0.3.28** + `pg`, Postgres only.

- Runtime wiring: `<root>/apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (`autoLoadEntities`, `synchronize: false`, pool `extra.max` from `resolveDbPoolSize` in `<root>/apps/api/src/common/db-pool.ts`).
- CLI DataSource: `<root>/apps/api/src/data-source.ts` — `entities: ['src/**/*.entity.ts']`, `migrations: ['src/migrations/*.ts']`, `migrationsTransactionMode: 'each'`, `uuidExtension: 'pgcrypto'`.
- Entities live per feature folder as `<feature>/entities/*.entity.ts`.

Migration workflow (`<root>/apps/api/package.json` scripts):
```
migration:run       pnpm typeorm migration:run -d src/data-source.ts
migration:revert    pnpm typeorm migration:revert -d src/data-source.ts
migration:generate  pnpm typeorm migration:generate -d src/data-source.ts
```
Generate is used as `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api migration:generate src/migrations/<Name>` (per CI's error text). Files land at `<root>/apps/api/src/migrations/<epochMillis>-<Name>.ts`, class `<Name><epochMillis>` with a `name` field. Existing set (7): `1784513040045-InitAuthSchema`, `1784519962991-AddMailboxMessages`, `1784566605863-AddNameInventoryAndPinnedCids`, `1784600557946-AddRecordCache`, `1784692000000-AddMailboxReceivedAtIndex`, `1784800000000-AddIdentitySubjects`, `1787155468460-AddDeviceApprovals`.

```ts
export class AddDeviceApprovals1787155468460 implements MigrationInterface {
  name = 'AddDeviceApprovals1787155468460';
```

Session/refresh table example — `refresh_tokens`, entity `RefreshToken`:
```ts
@Entity('refresh_tokens')
export class RefreshToken {
  @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid') id: string;
  @Index('idx_refresh_tokens_user_id')
  @Column({ name: 'user_id', type: 'uuid' }) userId: string;
  @Index('idx_refresh_tokens_family_id')
```

Other entities: `<root>/apps/api/src/auth/entities/{user,auth-method,identity-subject}.entity.ts`, `<root>/apps/api/src/device-approval/entities/{account-device,device-approval}.entity.ts`, `<root>/apps/api/src/mailbox/entities/mailbox-message.entity.ts`, `<root>/apps/api/src/registry/entities/{name-inventory,pinned-cid}.entity.ts`, `<root>/apps/api/src/republisher/entities/record-cache.entity.ts`.

### `pg_advisory_xact_lock`

Central helper: `<root>/apps/api/src/common/advisory-lock.ts`. Exports:
- `resolveAdvisoryLockTimeoutMs(configService): number` (env `DB_ADVISORY_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 3000, `0` = unbounded)
- `setAdvisoryLockTimeout(manager, timeoutMs)`, `isLockNotAvailable(error)` (`55P03`)
- `advisoryLockKey(token: string): bigint` — `sha256(token).readBigInt64BE(0)`
- `accountLockKey(accountId)` = `advisoryLockKey('account:' + id)`; `pinDurabilityLockKey(cid)`
- `acquireAdvisoryLocks(manager, keys: bigint[])` — dedupe + sort, then `SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(k) FROM unnest($1::bigint[]) AS k ORDER BY k`; `55P03` → `ServiceUnavailableException`

Consumers: `mailbox.service.ts`, `content.service.ts`, `registry/services/{registry,account}.service.ts`, `device-approval/services/{device-approval,account-device}.service.ts` (each defines a namespaced local key fn, e.g. `advisoryLockKey('device-approval:' + userId)`). **The auth module currently uses no advisory locks** — `TokenService.rotate` serializes via the atomic `update(... usedAt: IsNull())` claim instead. If your accelerator token mints inside rotation, note rotation is *not* in a transaction today.

---

## 4. Guards / strategies / `req.user`

No Passport. One JWT guard, hand-rolled.

`<root>/apps/api/src/auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts`:
```ts
export interface AuthenticatedUser { userId: string; publicKey?: string; scope?: TokenScope }
export type AuthenticatedRequest = Request & { user: AuthenticatedUser };
export function accountPublicKey(request: AuthenticatedRequest): string
@Injectable() export class JwtAuthGuard implements CanActivate {
  constructor(private readonly jwtService: JwtService, private readonly reflector: Reflector)
  async canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean>
  private assertScopeReaches(context, scope: TokenScope): void
}
```
`req.user` is set by the guard: `request.user = { userId: payload.sub, publicKey: payload.publicKey, scope }` from claims `{ sub, publicKey, scope? }`. Missing/non-`Bearer ` header → 401 `'Missing access token'`; verify failure → 401 `'Invalid access token'`.

Public routes: **there is no `@Public()` / `IS_PUBLIC_KEY` decorator.** `JwtAuthGuard` is opt-in per route or per class via `@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)`; anything undecorated is public. (Grep confirms the only `SetMetadata` in the codebase is `AllowScope`.)

Scope marking: `<root>/apps/api/src/auth/decorators/allow-scope.decorator.ts` — `export type TokenScope = 'device-approval'`, `ALLOWED_SCOPES_KEY = 'cipherbox:allowed-scopes'`, `AllowScope(...scopes: TokenScope[])`. Absence of the decorator = refusal for scoped tokens (fail-closed), handler-level overrides class-level via `reflector.getAllAndOverride`.

The only true global guard is the throttler: `<root>/apps/api/src/ops/ops.module.ts` binds `{ provide: APP_GUARD, useClass: AccountThrottlerGuard }` (`<root>/apps/api/src/ops/account-throttler.guard.ts`), which independently parses the bearer via `verifiedUnexpiredSubjectFromBearer(headers)` (also used by the raw-upload middleware in `app-setup.ts`) reading `JWT_SECRET` from `process.env` directly, outside DI. Per-surface limits: `THROTTLE_SURFACES` in `<root>/apps/api/src/ops/throttling.ts` (`auth` = `resolveAuthLimit()`/60s, `refresh` = 30/60s). A new lookup endpoint should add a named surface there.

| Unit | `src/**/*.test.ts` (excl. `*.scheduled.test.ts`) | `<root>/apps/api/vitest.config.ts` | `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api test` |

Rotation mechanics in `rotate()` (order matters):
1. `findOne({ where: { tokenHash } })`; miss → 401 `'Invalid refresh token'`.
2. `usedAt !== null` → **reuse**: `delete({ familyId })`, `logger.warn`, 401.
3. expired → `delete({ familyId })`, 401 `'Refresh token expired'`.
4. Atomic single-use claim: `update({ id, usedAt: IsNull() }, { usedAt: now })`; `!claim.affected` → delete family, 401.
5. Opportunistic sweep: `delete({ userId, expiresAt: LessThan(now) })`.
6. `publicKey = await publicKeyByUserId(userId)`; sign new access token; `mintRefreshToken(userId, existing.familyId)` (same family).


4. `requested > policy.staging_budget_bytes` → `Refusal::DeviceFull` (this device's measured budget).
5. `committed = staged.saturating_add(self.reserved())`; `available = policy.staging_budget_bytes.saturating_sub(committed)`; `requested > available` → `Refusal::Backlog`.

Otherwise it mints a `ReservationId` and inserts into `self.live`. const SW_FILE = 'sw.js';
```ts
const MANIFEST_FILE = 'precache-manifest.json';

/**
 * The app-shell pair, sharing one build id: the manifest the Service Worker
 * precaches on install — every emitted chunk, as same-origin absolute paths —
 * and the worker itself, stamped with a digest of those same bytes so the shell
 * cache rotates with the output.

 * scope is bounded by its own URL path — and as a classic script, not the ES
 * module the app's chunk graph would emit.
 */
function appShell(): Plugin[] {
  let buildId: string | null = null;

  return [
    {
      name: 'cipherbox:precache-manifest',
      enforce: 'post',
      generateBundle(_options, bundle) {
        const fileNames = Object.keys(bundle)
          .filter((fileName) => !fileName.endsWith('.map'))
          .sort();

        const digest = createHash('sha256');
        for (const fileName of fileNames) {
          const output = bundle[fileName];
          digest.update(fileName);
          digest.update(output.type === 'chunk' ? output.code : output.source);
        }
        buildId = digest.digest('hex').slice(0, 16);

        const shell = fileNames.map((fileName) => `/${fileName}`);
        this.emitFile({
          type: 'asset',
          fileName: MANIFEST_FILE,
          source: `${JSON.stringify(shell, null, 2)}\n`,
        });
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'cipherbox:service-worker',
      apply: 'build',
      async closeBundle() {
        if (buildId === null)
          throw new Error('the precache manifest emitted no app-shell build id');
        await build({
          configFile: false,
          logLevel: 'warn',
          define: { __APP_SHELL_BUILD_ID__: JSON.stringify(buildId) },
          build: {
            outDir: OUT_DIR,
            emptyOutDir: false,
            rollupOptions: {
              input: SW_ENTRY,
              // `iife` keeps the classic-script contract: an `es` chunk reaching for
              // a dynamic import emits `import.meta`, which a classic worker rejects.
              output: { entryFileNames: SW_FILE, codeSplitting: false, format: 'iife' },

        });

        // to install, and the shell it precached is never rotated.
        const emitted = await readFile(join(OUT_DIR, SW_FILE), 'utf8');
```

```rust
pub const JOURNAL_GC_MAX_AGE_DAYS: u64 = 30;
```

The status enum (v1 `crates/sdk/src/queue.rs:166-177`):
```rust
pub enum JournalEntryStatus {
    Pending,       // Awaiting first upload attempt.
    InProgress,    // Upload attempt currently in progress.
    /// All retries exhausted; entry parked on disk for manual intervention (D-09).
    Failed { last_error: String },
```

The eviction routine, `gc_failed_entries(age_days, total_size_budget)` (v1 `crates/sdk/src/queue.rs:463-591`). Its doc comment is the exact rationale the v2 blueprint is missing:
> Parked `Failed` entries are kept on disk for manual intervention (D-09) and would otherwise grow without bound, exhausting disk (T-52-16, Denial of Service). This runs once per mount and is best-effort — per-file errors are logged and skipped, never fatal. Three passes, all touching ONLY `Failed` entries (in-flight `Pending`/`InProgress` are never GC'd):
> 1. **Age purge** — remove any `Failed` entry whose `created_at_ms` is older than `age_days` …
> 2. **Size purge** — sum each surviving `Failed` entry's on-disk size (`.json` bytes plus its `.bin` sidecar bytes); if the total exceeds `total_size_budget`, remove oldest-first (by `created_at_ms`) until under budget.
> 3. **Orphan cleanup** — delete any `.bin` sidecar with no matching `<id>.json` (a sidecar left behind by an aborted write, RESEARCH Pitfall 2).

```ts
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import { build, loadEnv, type Plugin } from 'vite';
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

import { missingDeployEnv, shipsE2eHook } from './src/engine/config';

const OUT_DIR = fileURLToPath(new URL('dist', import.meta.url));
const SW_ENTRY = fileURLToPath(new URL('src/sw.ts', import.meta.url));
const SW_FILE = 'sw.js';
const MANIFEST_FILE = 'precache-manifest.json';

/**
 * The app-shell pair, sharing one build id: the manifest the Service Worker
 * precaches on install — every emitted chunk, as same-origin absolute paths —
 * and the worker itself, stamped with a digest of those same bytes so the shell
 * cache rotates with the output.
 *
 * The worker is a second pass so it lands unhashed at the output root — its
 * scope is bounded by its own URL path — and as a classic script, not the ES
 * module the app's chunk graph would emit.
 */
function appShell(): Plugin[] {
  let buildId: string | null = null;

  return [
    {
      name: 'cipherbox:precache-manifest',
      enforce: 'post',
      generateBundle(_options, bundle) {
        const fileNames = Object.keys(bundle)
          .filter((fileName) => !fileName.endsWith('.map'))
          .sort();

        const digest = createHash('sha256');
        for (const fileName of fileNames) {
          const output = bundle[fileName];
          digest.update(fileName);
          digest.update(output.type === 'chunk' ? output.code : output.source);
        }
        buildId = digest.digest('hex').slice(0, 16);

        const shell = fileNames.map((fileName) => `/${fileName}`);
        this.emitFile({
          type: 'asset',
          fileName: MANIFEST_FILE,
          source: `${JSON.stringify(shell, null, 2)}\n`,
        });
      },
    },
    {
      name: 'cipherbox:service-worker',
      apply: 'build',
      async closeBundle() {
        if (buildId === null)
          throw new Error('the precache manifest emitted no app-shell build id');
        await build({
          configFile: false,
          logLevel: 'warn',
          define: { __APP_SHELL_BUILD_ID__: JSON.stringify(buildId) },
          build: {
            outDir: OUT_DIR,
            emptyOutDir: false,
            rollupOptions: {
              input: SW_ENTRY,
              // `iife` keeps the classic-script contract: an `es` chunk reaching for
              // a dynamic import emits `import.meta`, which a classic worker rejects.
              output: { entryFileNames: SW_FILE, codeSplitting: false, format: 'iife' },
            },
          },
        });
        // The worker's bytes must vary per deploy or the browser finds no update
        // to install, and the shell it precached is never rotated.
        const emitted = await readFile(join(OUT_DIR, SW_FILE), 'utf8');
        if (!emitted.includes(buildId)) throw new Error(`${SW_FILE} did not take the build stamp`);
      },
    },
  ];
}

/**
 * Fails a deployment build whose login-critical environment is unset, or one
 * that would ship the e2e introspection hook.
 */
function deployEnvGate(): Plugin {
  return {
    name: 'cipherbox:deploy-env-gate',
    apply: 'build',
    config(_config, { mode }) {
      const env = loadEnv(mode, import.meta.dirname, 'VITE_');
      const missing = missingDeployEnv(env);
      if (missing.length > 0) {
        throw new Error(
          `a ${env.VITE_ENVIRONMENT} build cannot log in without ${missing.join(', ')}`
        );
      }
      if (shipsE2eHook(env)) {
        throw new Error(`a ${env.VITE_ENVIRONMENT} build must not set VITE_E2E_HOOK`);
      }
    },
  };
}

export default defineConfig({

    },
  },
  test: {
    environment: 'jsdom',
    setupFiles: ['./src/test/setup.ts'],
    include: ['src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}'],
  },
});
```

```ts
  command: `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web exec vite preview --outDir ${outDir} --port ${port} --strictPort`,
  url: url(port),
```

with `const E2E_PORT = 4173;` / `const RELEASE_PORT = 4174;`, and the header comment: *"Both projects run against the production static build, served from a built directory — the artifact that ships is the artifact tested."*

**Would a CSP in `preview.headers` apply during the suite? Yes.** The command runs `vite preview` via `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web exec`, so the working directory is `apps/web` and Vite loads `apps/web/vite.config.ts`. A `preview: { headers: { 'Content-Security-Policy': ... } }` block would be served on every response from both preview servers, so the e2e suite would genuinely exercise the policy. This is the single highest-value place to put a CSP if you want it tested rather than merely deployed — today `preview` is entirely absent from the config, so the suite runs with **no** CSP and **no** COOP, i.e. it does not currently validate the Caddy policy at all.

Caveats to be aware of if you add `preview.headers`:
- `vite preview` is invoked with `--outDir dist` / `--outDir dist-release` but no `--outDir`-independent config override, so both servers get the same headers.
- Playwright is pinned to `channel: 'chromium'` (real Chrome headless, not `chrome-headless-shell`) specifically because the shell segfaults on SW registration — so SW + precache behavior under CSP is genuinely exercised.
- `release-bundle.spec.ts` asserts `navigator.serviceWorker.controller?.scriptURL` matches `/\/sw\.js$/`, so a `worker-src`/`script-src` that blocks the SW would fail loudly. Good.
- CI env in `.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml` points the bundle at `VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000`, `VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS: http://localhost:3001` (mock someguy), `VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8080` (Kubo gateway). **An enumerated `connect-src` in `preview.headers` would have to allow these `http://localhost:*` / `http://127.0.0.1:*` origins**, or every write/read spec fails. This is the main friction point for a `connect-src`-bearing preview CSP; a `frame-ancestors 'none'`-only policy has no such problem.
- `vite preview` serves no `Service-Worker-Allowed` header today either, but the built `/sw.js` is at the root so it needs none.

## Where invite-link records are stored

**Not in `Engine` state.** They live in the durable staging seam, opened per call:

- Store type: `StagingInviteStore<'a, St, E>` — `crates/engine/src/grants/invite_store.rs:264`
  - fields: `staging: &'a St`, `enc_secret: &'a X25519Secret`, `entropy: &'a RefCell<E>`, `staging_key: Vec<u8>`
  - `StagingInviteStore::new(staging, enc_secret, entropy)`; `staging_key()` → the one key holding the whole set
  - key namespace: `pub const INVITE_RECORDS_PREFIX: &[u8] = b"cbx/iv/"` (invite_store.rs:66), owner-scoped via `owner_scoped_key(...)`
  - sealed with `seal_owner_local(..., OwnerLocalKind::InviteRecords, ...)`
- Trait: `pub trait InviteStore { async fn persist(&self, records: &InviteRecords) -> Result<(), InviteStoreError>; async fn load(&self) -> Result<InviteRecords, InviteStoreError>; }` (invite_store.rs:184–197). Whole-set replacement.

Record shapes:

```rust
// invite_store.rs:157
pub struct InviteRecords {
    pub links: Vec<RecordedInvite>,
    pub claims: Vec<ConvertedClaimRecord>,
}
impl InviteRecords { pub fn forget_links(&mut self, tags: &BTreeSet<[u8; 32]>) }  // :174

// invite.rs:256
pub struct RecordedInvite {          // Copy
    pub tag: [u8; 32],                                  // blinded tag; the link's identity
    pub ephemeral_identity_pk: [u8; IDENTITY_PUBLIC_LEN],
    pub ephemeral_enc_pk: [u8; SECRET_LEN],
    pub expires_at: Option<UnixMillis>,                 // this copy is the authority
}

// invite.rs:431
pub struct ConvertedClaimRecord {    // Copy
    pub claim_id: [u8; CLAIM_ID_LEN],   // CLAIM_ID_LEN = 16
    pub link_tag: [u8; 32],
    pub tag: [u8; 32],                  // the personal grant the conversion minted
}
```

Caps: `MAX_INVITE_RECORDS = 1024`, `MAX_CONVERTED_CLAIMS = 4096` (invite_store.rs:80, 85).

**Important for your feature:** there is **no claim count, no per-link node/scope id, and no facade read that enumerates minted links.** A record carries only `tag`, the two ephemeral pubkeys, and `expires_at`. Which node a link belongs to is recovered only by `link_binds_scope(enc_secret, link, &ipns_name)` (invite.rs:802) / `locate_invite_link(...)` (invite.rs:819) against a resolved scope root — that is how `revoke_invite_link` and `prune_invite_links` find "the link at this node". So "does this folder have a live link?" is not currently answerable by a read; it is only answerable by a resolve.

# 4. `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts` — the wire protocol

Four discriminated unions matter. **Adding a method means touching all of: `CommandDescriptor` here, `buildCommand` in `commandCodec.ts`, and a `Command.*` builder in `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs`.** A new *read* additionally needs `WorkerRequest` here, `EngineTransport` + `LocalTransport` in `transport.ts`, `EngineHostLike` + `EngineHost` in `engineHost.ts`, the `WireRead` union in `broadcast.ts`, `broadcastTransport.ts`, and `leaderRelay.ts`.

## `CommandDescriptor` (:212–249) — invite entries verbatim

```ts

      kind: 'createInviteLink';
      node: Uint8Array;
      permission: Permission;
      /** Unix-millis deadline; `null` mints a link that never expires. */
      expiresAt: bigint | null;

  | { kind: 'revokeInviteLink'; node: Uint8Array }
```

## Decision: #1355 — how a carried field declares itself uncuttable

**The question.** `crates/core/src/seal/envelope.rs:111` protects exactly two carried fields from the size-pressure cut, by hard-coded name: `grantSection` and `writeSealed`. That list freezes when v2.0 binaries ship. A v2.0 reader can never learn that a later additive field is protocol-bearing, so it would cut that field silently. We must decide now: reserve a wire-level way for a future field to declare itself uncuttable, or write down that no additive envelope field will ever be protocol-bearing.

**Key facts from the code:**

- Map keys are free UTF-8 with length-first ordering (`codec/value.rs:190-194`). A one-byte `!` prefix is representable today and no reserved key uses it.
- Rotation carries envelope unknowns verbatim (`net/rotation.rs:865` and 4 more sites). Envelope bloat is relieved only by the cut, so a publisher-declared marker without a byte budget hands a hostile publisher a permanent uncuttable pad.
- The precedent for a frozen byte bound exists: `MAX_WRITE_BODY_BYTES` at `seal/write_body.rs:351-365`, frozen in `kat/manifest.json:300`.
- Interior envelopes have no uncuttable field at all, and a foreign envelope `v` is rejected outright (`net/rotation.rs:721`, `:1212`). So a `v` bump is a hard fork, not a graceful path.

**The options:**

- **A — reserved `!` key-name prefix + a frozen critical-bytes budget.** Costs 1 byte per future critical field, ~40 lines, 2-3 tests, KAT vectors, one blueprint paragraph. Works at top level and inside `epochTag`. The budget must ship with the marker, symmetric and release-active at both `decode_envelope` and `encode_envelope`, or the marker is worse than today. This option makes **#1356** (grant-section byte bound) a hard prerequisite — size both bounds in one sitting.
- **B — reserved `"critical"` sub-map.** Smallest code delta, but ~11 bytes of framing per record forever, all-or-nothing granularity, and every nested map needs its own future reservation. Same #1356 prerequisite.
- **C — prohibit protocol-bearing additive fields; change nothing.** Zero cost now. But interior nodes then can never gain a protocol-bearing additive field — the `revocationPin` example in #1355 becomes impossible without a per-node hard fork.

**Sub-decision:** keep largest-first cut ranking (`envelope.rs:175`). Under A the marker closes the one adversary largest-first leaves open.

**My recommendation: Option A, paired with #1356 in one PR or with #1356 first, largest-first kept.** C's cost lands on interior nodes and is unrecoverable after the freeze. B is A with a worse footprint.

**Conflict check:** no open PRs; no wave-15 worktree touches `crates/core`. One soft overlap: W15-1 edits `sync/drain.rs`, which owns the cut report — sequence #1355 implementation after W15-1, do not parallelize.

## 1. `evict_over_budget` reads every kept root on every preserve — up to 17 seam round trips where 0 are needed

**`/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a1a341862fef22d8c/crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs:253-256`**

```rust
let mut sizes = Vec::with_capacity(kept.len());
for record in kept.iter() {
    sizes.push(preserved_version_bytes(store, record).await);
}
```

`preserved_version_bytes` (line 223) does its own `staged_bytes(&root)` per record. The loop runs unconditionally, before any check of whether either cap is exceeded — so the common case (3 preserved, well under budget, evicting nothing) still pays 4 root reads and 4 `decode_root` calls to compute a total it then discards. At steady state (`MAX_PRESERVED_DEAD_LETTERS = 16` held, one more appended) it is **17 reads**.

Cost of one `preserve_dead_letter` on a Kept path with a full set:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `staged_bytes(PRESERVED_KEY)` | 1 | 1 |
| `staged_keys()` (full listing) | 0 | **1** |
| `staged_bytes(root)` | 0 | **18** (1 coherence + 17 sizing) |
| `put_staged_bytes` | 1 | 1 |
| **total** | **2** | **21+**, plus the eviction release below |

The sizes are pure derived data the engine already knew when each record was preserved. The preserved blob is this module's own format (`PRESERVED_FORMAT_V1`, tag + `u32` length prefix, lines 306-325) — bumping to a v2 that carries a `u64` size beside each length prefix costs 8 bytes/entry and drops the sweep to **zero** reads: sizes for the existing 16 come off the blob, and the new entry's size comes free from finding 2 below. Alternatively keep a running total under a sibling key. Either way the eviction decision becomes arithmetic on already-loaded bytes.

Note there is no cheap short-circuit available here (you cannot know `total > budget` without all sizes), so memoization is the fix, not reordering.

## 2. The newly-preserved record's root is read and decoded twice, back to back

**`staging.rs:168-173` then `staging.rs:178` → `223-237`**

`version_is_coherent` does `staged_bytes(root_cid)` + `verify_cid` + `decode_root`, and the `manifest` it obtains holds exactly `.size` and `.leaf_cids.len()` — the two fields `preserved_version_bytes` then re-reads and re-decodes the *same* root block to get, milliseconds later in the same call.

Cost: **1 redundant `staged_bytes` + 1 redundant BLAKE3 `verify_cid` + 1 redundant `decode_root` per preserve**. For a 1 GiB version at 1 MiB leaves the root manifest is ~37 KB, so that is a ~37 KB read and a ~37 KB hash thrown away — synchronous CPU on the engine's current-thread executor.

Cheaper: have `version_is_coherent` return `Option<RootManifest>` (or a small `(coherent, bytes)` pair) instead of `bool`, and thread it into the append. Free — no restructuring.

## 3. `release_version_blocks` re-reads a root the caller just decoded, in both new eviction paths

**`staging.rs:265-269`** (eviction) and **`staging.rs:431-434`** (prune)

`release_version_blocks` (line 101) → `version_leaf_cids` (line 112) → `staged_bytes(root_cid)` + `verify_cid` + `decode_root`. But:

- in `evict_over_budget`, `preserved_version_bytes` already read and decoded that exact root one loop earlier to size it;
- in `prune_preserved_dead_letters`, `version_is_coherent` at line 422 already read and decoded that exact root to classify it hollow.

Cost: **+1 `staged_bytes` + 1 `verify_cid` + 1 `decode_root` per evicted/hollow record**, on top of the L `remove_staged_bytes` calls that are genuinely needed.

Cheaper: add a `release_leaves(store, root_cid, leaves: &[Vec<u8>])` taking the already-decoded leaf list, with `release_version_blocks` remaining the fetch-then-release wrapper for callers that have nothing in hand. (In prune's root-missing case there is no manifest to reuse, and there the current re-read costs nothing — `staged_bytes` returns `None` and `version_leaf_cids` bails.)

## 4. `collect_orphans` now does two full `staged_keys()` listings per pass

**`staging.rs:412`**, inside `prune_preserved_dead_letters`, called from `collect_orphans` at **`staging.rs:401`**

On desktop that is a second `read_dir` of the staged directory (`crates/desktop-seams/src/staging_store.rs:161`); on web it is a second OPFS async directory iteration plus a WASM↔JS marshal of ~1,000 `Uint8Array`s (`packages/client/src/seams/stagingStore.ts:212`).

## 1. `version_is_coherent` vs the drain's upload loop — not one rule, two that disagree

They are two expressions of *one invariant* ("the missing leaves are exactly the confirmed-uploaded prefix"), implemented against **different evidence**, and they are not equivalent predicates.

The drain's rule, evidence = the durable mark:

> held set ⊇ every leaf at index ≥ `uploaded`

The new rule, evidence = shape alone:

> held set is a contiguous suffix (no held leaf may precede a missing one)

Two concrete divergences, both reachable:

**(a) The shape rule is strictly stricter, and the drain documents the exact case it rejects.** `drain.rs:2185-2188`: *"A leaf a lost release left staged behind the mark is re-uploaded here"* — i.e. held `{0, 3, 4, 5}` with `uploaded == 3` is a state the loop explicitly handles as fine. `version_is_coherent` sees held-then-missing and returns `false` → `ContentGone` → the caller releases the whole version and reports `ContentUnrecoverable`. Those leaves 3-5 were the *only* local copy of the recoverable tail of a version whose prefix is pinned on the network (the `AttemptsExhausted` path deliberately retires only the name, `drain.rs:798-802`). So a stranded-release artifact turns a recoverable dead letter into a destroyed one, reported to the user as unrecoverable.

**(b) The shape rule is also strictly weaker in the all-leaves-missing case.** `held_one` never flips, so the loop falls through to `true` — a version with zero leaves and a live root is "coherent". That is indistinguishable, from shape, between "fully uploaded, publish failed" (recoverable) and "the prefix was evicted/deleted" (the exact condition `UPLOAD_MARK_KEY`'s doc at `drain.rs:322-326` says the mark exists to detect). The mark can tell these apart; the shape cannot.

**Why the depth is wrong:** the invariant's real statement needs a *progress number*, and the fix chose to infer it from the arrangement of bytes rather than read it. That is the bandaid shape — it works on the happy path and silently mis-answers on precisely the two edges the drain already enumerated.

**Deeper fix, and the right home:** staging.rs. It already owns the suffix invariant on the *producing* side (`release_version_blocks`, `staging.rs:96-106`: "File order keeps the blocks that remain a suffix at every step, which is the invariant the drain's resume reads"). Name the *reading* side there too, as one function over one evidence set:

```rust
enum StagedProgress { Confirmed(usize), Hole }
fn staged_progress(manifest: &Root, held: &HashSet<Vec<u8>>, mark: Option<usize>) -> StagedProgress
```

`upload_blocks` consumes it and maps `Hole → CONTENT_LOST`; `preserve_dead_letter` and the prune consume it and map `Hole → ContentGone`. The *destination* semantics of the mark (`Destinations`, `mirror_gap`) stay in drain — those are placement, not staging.

There is a real obstacle you should know about before proposing that: `UPLOAD_MARK_KEY` is **single-slot, keyed to the head content op's root** (`drain.rs:320-329`, `decode_upload_mark` returns `Resume::default()` on root mismatch). - Soft-delete means: the `FolderChild` is **removed from its parent folder's children array** and the verbatim child object is **copied into the bin blob**. The underlying file-metadata IPNS record and content CID are left untouched and still pinned.

Three paths, all sharing one helper.

- `permanentDeleteFromBin` — `v1:packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:748-778`

- `purgeExpiredEntries` — `:822-863`

**Recursion happens at soft-delete time, not at purge time.** The doc comment on the helper records the bug this fixed (`v1:packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:305-311`):

> "Shared by emptyBin, permanentDeleteFromBin and purgeExpiredEntries so all three paths unpin the SAME set (the prior bug: the first two only looked at `entry.contentCid` and never looped `versionCids`/`descendantCids`)."

> ```
>  * Recursively walk a deleted folder subtree, collecting every node's IPNS name

>  *

>  * or decrypted, the whole walk THROWS — addToBin must then abort the delete
>  * rather than half-revoke / partially unpin. This is what guarantees the share
>  * set is complete before the destructive folder mutation. (An individual file's

**Client-side (zero-knowledge preserved):**
- The entire bin data structure. No DB table, no bin endpoint. Server sees only an opaque ECIES blob CID + an IPNS record it can't correlate to a vault.
- Retention setting and expiry evaluation.
- Subtree enumeration, CID capture, name-collision resolution, re-encryption.

**`loadBin` must never publish on a null resolve** — the longest and most emphatic comment in the file, `v1:packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:336-356`:

## Result: no high-confidence exploitable vulnerabilities introduced by this PR

I found nothing meeting the >80%-confidence bar. Below is what I checked and why each candidate cleared.

### SQL injection / query construction
`apps/api/src/auth/services/gateway-token.service.ts:102-124`. Both query builders are fully parameter-bound:
- The raw join string `'refresh.family_id = gateway.family_id AND refresh.used_at IS NULL AND refresh.expires_at > :now'` contains no interpolation; `:now` is supplied via `.setParameter('now', new Date(now))`, which TypeORM resolves at `getQuery()` time and applies to join conditions as well as `WHERE`.
- `:tokenHash` is bound, and is in any case a locally computed SHA-256 hex — no attacker bytes reach SQL.
- The identifiers used in raw form (`gateway.token_hash`, `gateway.expires_at`, `refresh.*`) are all-lowercase snake_case that match the real column names, so Postgres resolves them against the quoted aliases correctly. The delete builder in `mintForFamily` (`:userId`, `:tokenHash`, `:familyId`, `:now`) is likewise bound.

### Derived-liveness join — can it accept a revoked session?
I traced every path that ends a session in `apps/api/src/auth/services/token.service.ts`:
- logout → `revokeAllForUser` hard-deletes all refresh rows for the user;
- reuse detection and expiry → `delete({ familyId })`;
- account delete → FK `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `gateway_tokens.user_id`;
- rotation → old row gets `used_at`, and `mintForFamily`'s sweep deletes the family's prior gateway row.

In every case the `used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > :now` join fails, or the gateway row is gone. There is no per-family logout that could leave a live refresh row behind a revoked session. `family_id` is never attacker-supplied (either `entropy.randomUuid()` or copied from the existing row), so the missing `refresh.user_id = gateway.user_id` predicate is not reachable — it would require a v4 UUID collision. The rotation race window (between marking `used_at` and inserting the successor) fails *closed*, not open.

### Token strength, comparison, and shape gate
`entropy.randomBytes(32)` → `SystemEntropy` → `node:crypto.randomBytes` (`apps/api/src/common/entropy.ts`), wired as the production binding in `apps/api/src/common/runtime.module.ts`. 256 bits, hex-encoded. `HEX_32_BYTES_RE` has no `g` flag (no `lastIndex` statefulness) and is lowercase-only, matching the mint output exactly. Lookup is an indexed unique-column match on the SHA-256 digest — timing is not a usable oracle against a 256-bit random preimage. Cross-table confusion (refresh token ↔ gateway token, identical shape and hash function) is impossible because each lookup targets its own table.

### Endpoint data exposure
`apps/api/src/auth/gateway.controller.ts:44-49` returns bare 204/401. The two 401 messages distinguish only "no header" from "header present but rejected" — no account, user, or existence signal. The shape gate short-circuits before the DB, which leaks only the publicly known token shape. No logging of the raw token anywhere: the only `Logger` line in the auth path (`token.service.ts:120`) predates this PR and prints ids, not secrets.

### Rust side — cell separation
`crates/engine/src/api/client.rs:641-642` maps `access_token → session` and `gateway_token → accelerator`; the API leg reads only `self.session` (`client.rs:563`) and the gateway leg only its own `SessionBearer` (`crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:383`). `clear_session` clears both; `facade.rs` seals both on shutdown. `GatewayConfig::into_gateway` (`read.rs:227-238`) still gives the bearer to the accelerator source alone — public fallbacks get `SessionBearer::default()`, and the pre-existing TLS-only restriction on the accelerator URL is untouched. Both legs build the header through `bearer_header` (`crates/engine/src/seams/http.rs:51`), which validates the token charset, so a hostile API response cannot CRLF-inject via the new `gatewayToken` field any more than via `accessToken`.

### Config / cache trust window
`positiveIntConfig` (`apps/api/src/common/config-int.ts`) fails closed to the default on `NaN`, non-integral, `<= 0`, or over-max — so `GATEWAY_TOKEN_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` is hard-capped at 60s and cannot be widened by garbage input. Accepted entries are additionally clamped by `Math.min(live.expires_at.getTime(), now + cacheTtlMs)`, so a cache entry can never outlive its row. `resolveAccessTtlSeconds` has no `max`, but it governed the access JWT's `expiresIn` before this PR under the same unboundedness — and it now fails closed to 900 where the old `Number(...)` would have produced `NaN`, which is a net improvement.

### One accepted-risk note (below reporting threshold, not a finding)
The in-process accept cache means a token whose session was revoked keeps opening the gateway for up to `GATEWAY_TOKEN_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` (10s default, 60s max). This is stated as intentional in `blueprint/api.md` ("the verify endpoint's in-process cache bounds how long a revoked token is still honoured") and in the contract test's own comment, requires the attacker to already hold the token, and yields only E2EE bytes. Flagging it as awareness rather than a vulnerability.

Excluded per scope: the `@SkipThrottle()` on the verify route, the missing `family_id` index on `gateway_tokens`, and the cache-eviction spray — all DoS/rate-limiting shaped.</result>

The pseudonym is `entropy.randomBytes(32).toString('hex')` (`gateway-token.service.ts:68`) — pure CSPRNG, no derivation from `publicKey`, `userId`, `familyId`, or anything in the KDF edge catalog. `SystemEntropy` wraps `node:crypto` `randomBytes` and is the production binding (`common/runtime.module.ts:10`); `FakeEntropy` is test-only. 256 bits is well above any guessing budget.

**Unsalted SHA-256 is the right choice here, not a defect.** Argon2/bcrypt exist to buy work factor against *low-entropy* secrets; against a uniform 256-bit token there is no dictionary and no rainbow table to defend against, so a salt buys nothing and a KDF would put ~100ms on the system's highest-frequency route. # Decision brief — #1399, the recycle bin as vault-level engine behavior

**Grounding:** `main` @ `3d3ac0fc1`. The existing proposal comment on #1399 was grounded at `243c6ce74` (5 commits back); its claims verify but many line numbers have drifted — corrected numbers are used throughout.

## (a) The question

The bin does not exist anywhere in `crates/engine`, `crates/core`, `packages/client`, or `apps/web`, yet `blueprint/web-client.md:266` commits `/bin` with "restore/purge ops via facade" and `blueprint/desktop.md:192-194` calls the bin "vault-level engine behavior." The decision is where a deleted node's *state* lives between delete and purge, and what rebase, rotation, and reclamation rules that placement inherits.

**No frozen decision constrains this.** The blueprint cites `FSM1/cipher-box-next#5` for recycle-bin semantics, but #5 is the v1 feature keep/cut list and never mentions the bin — the citation only carries "nothing shipped in v1 was cut except vault import." This is open design.

## Four findings that reshape the problem

**F1 — Today's delete is already half a bin, and a revocation hole.** `publish_delete` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:1330-1356`) drops one `ChildRef` and republishes the parent. The child's record is never retired (the only `retire(...)` sites in drain.rs are `2615`/`2636`/`2663`, none on the delete path), its `HeldRecords` entry is never evicted (`drain.rs:2578` is the *only* mutation of `held` in the whole crate), and content is never unpinned (`release_staged_blocks`, `drain.rs:2329-2334`, early-returns because a `Delete` op yields no content root, `op.rs:434-446`). That is #1434. **The unstated consequence: an unlinked-but-live node is unreachable from the tree, so it is in no eager set (`CONTEXT.md:21`) and no sweep. A revoked grantee holding the old scope seed keeps reading every deleted node forever.** That is a fail-open revocation residual on `main` today, and it is the decisive argument in D1 below.

**F2 — The rebase rule collides, and nobody has noticed.** `Delete` today rebases under *conditional delete* — dropped if the target advanced, edit wins, "a rebased edit resurrects a concurrently deleted node" (`blueprint/engine.md:400`, `CONTEXT.md:60`, code at `sync/rebase.rs:503`). `Move` rebases under a different rule entirely — dest-first publish, presence-conditional source-remove, race loser compensates (`blueprint/engine.md:404`, `publish_ref_move` at `drain.rs:1363`, source check at `drain.rs:1387-1389`). Repointing `Delete` at a relink-into-bin silently swaps one blueprint-locked rebase rule for another, and `blueprint/desktop.md:199` explicitly promises the FS core renders "edit-wins deletes." This needs an explicit decision (D5), not a side effect.

**F3 — A repointed `Delete` fills the bin with `.DS_Store`.** FUSE `rmdir` refuses a non-empty folder (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:1137-1155`) but treats platform junk as invisible, then `delete_descendants` issues **one `Command::Delete` per junk descendant** (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:1027-1046`). Repoint `Delete` and every hidden junk file the mount sweeps becomes a user-visible bin entry.

**F4 — v1's bin was not a folder at all**, which is a fourth model the proposal never weighed: a standalone per-user JSON blob, ECIES-sealed, published at an IPNS name HKDF-derived from the login secret (`v1:packages/core/src/bin/derive-ipns.ts:19-21`), holding `BinEntry` records with `originalParentIpnsName`, `originalPath`, `deletedAt`, `descendantCids`, and `originalFolderKeyEncrypted` (`v1:packages/core/src/bin/types.ts:19-73`). v2 has the exact structural precedent for it — the vault settings record (`crates/engine/src/settings.rs`, 1719 lines; core framing at `crates/core/src/seal/settings_record.rs`, body opaque to core) and the owner-local store family (`crates/core/src/seal/owner_local.rs`, `OwnerLocalKind::{ReceivedShares, ContactBook, InviteRecords}`). It is a real option, and F1 is what kills it.

---

## (b) Sub-decisions

### D1 — Where deleted entries live

| Option | Mechanism | Pro | Con |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Bin root per scope** (reserved `NodeId`, ordinary folder child of the scope root; trash = intra-scope relink) | `OpKind::Move`/`Relink` under `ScopeCrossing::Intra` already exists and is the only crossing that publishes (`facade.rs:3685`, `:3713`; `drain.rs:1228` halts every other) | Node seeds are id-derived and location-independent (`CONTEXT.md:7`), so trash and restore are **pure relinks — no re-seal, no epoch change, no new KDF edge**. Binned nodes stay in the scope subtree, so they ride the lazy wave and re-seal on revocation — **this is the only option that closes F1.** `/bin` gets a per-scope listing free from `snapshot(binRoot)`; only the cross-scope union is new | Binned items are visible to that scope's grantees — deleting a shared file moves it to a shared trash. "Vault-level" becomes a facade aggregation, not a storage property. Needs a reserved-id mint guard and origin metadata (D2) |
| **B. Owner-sealed bin index; node stays unlinked-but-live** (v1's model, over the settings-record or owner-local pattern) | `settings.rs` / `received_share_store.rs` are working templates; delete path unchanged | Literally vault-level, one flat list. Owner-only by construction — no grantee disclosure. **Zero change to `publish_delete`, to the conditional-delete rebase rule, and no F3 regression.** Core cost near zero (both structures seal an engine-encoded body core never interprets) | **Fatal on F1**: a node absent from the tree is in no eager set and no sweep, so revocation never cuts access to anything binned. Also: the owner-local family rides the *per-device* `StagingStore` (`received_share_store.rs:1-10`), so it needs the published settings-record machinery instead — and that reintroduces v1's worst flaw, a whole-list rewrite with no CAS (`v1:packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:336-356` documents the resulting data-loss bug at length). Restore also needs a relink of a node absent from `Snapshot`, which no op supports. A grantee's delete lands in the grantee's private bin — the owner loses the file with no way to see it |
| **C. Tombstone on `ChildRef` in place** | New `deleted` field in the read-body | Restore trivial; origin metadata structurally free | Every read path must filter, and one that forgets is a **fail-open disclosure**. `/bin` has no index, so the vault-level listing is structurally incomplete. Adds a semantic field to the most-read structure in the wire format |
| **D. One vault-level bin scope** | — | Matches the words in the blueprint exactly | Unbuildable in v2.0. Every delete becomes a cross-scope move — refused at journal time (`refuse_scope_exit`, `facade.rs:1675-1686`, `ScopeExitRefused` at `:1152`) and at publish time (`drain.rs:1228`) — and per `CONTEXT.md:11`/`:21` a scope exit out of a granted scope is **a rotation per delete**. `consume_scope_exit_triggers` (`rotation/trigger.rs:106`) has zero production callers; `ReplayReport::scope_exit_triggers` (`rebase.rs:183`) is populated and dropped |

### D2 — Where origin metadata lives (only live under A)

| Option | Pro | Con |
|---|---|---|
| **Optional `origin` on `ChildRef`** `{parentId, name, deletedAt}` | Sealed inside the read-body, so it discloses nothing; renders in the listing with no resolve. `Map::insert` is canonically ordered by construction (`crates/core/src/codec/value.rs:224-233`), so ordering is free | One core wire change: accept + reject vectors, `manifest.json:207`/`:211` count bumps against the drift assert (`kat_manifest.rs:2165-2169`, `:2210-2213`), a reject `check` string pinned by `every_crate_check_is_pinned_by_a_vault_family` (`kat_manifest.rs:1704-1711`), and an AGENTS.md rule-8 release-active encode check matching `assert_children_unique` (`core/src/seal/body.rs:397-412`). Core gates engine, so it serializes the slices |
| **Ride `ChildRef.unknown` (`PreservedFields`)** | Genuinely zero-core — `collect_unknown`/`merge_unknown` (`body.rs:505-525`) round-trip byte-stably and typed fields always win | It *is* a wire format, with no schema, no acceptance domain, no reject vectors. Abuses the forward-compat channel. Same objection as encoding origin into the name string |
| **Owner-local side index for origin only** | No core change | Per-device (`StagingStore`), so origin is lost on the other device; and unreadable to a grantee restoring from a shared bin |

### D3 — Retention and what triggers a purge

The AC sketch on #1399 says "retention expiry is driven by the injected clock seam." That contradicts #1094's recorded decision (count-based keep-latest-N, no clock, declined age-based rules for replay determinism) and needs reconciling.

The engine reads its clock seam (`trait Scheduler`, `crates/engine/src/seams/scheduler.rs:50`) **exactly once per command**, at `facade.rs:3651`, journaled onto the op (`op.rs:43`), and every downstream publish reuses `applied.op.authored_at.0` (`drain.rs:1276, 1302, 1317, 1350, 1394, 1627, 2169`). So `deletedAt` is *data* and the UI may freely display "deleted 12 days ago"; the question is only whether the engine may **branch** on `now()` to destroy data.

| Option | Pro | Con |
|---|---|---|
| **User-initiated purge only** | Matches the existing blueprint rule verbatim — `blueprint/engine.md:796-797`: "Retention default: keep all versions within quota, with an explicit **user-initiated prune op**." No determinism question. No data destroyed without a gesture | The bin grows against quota until emptied |
| **Count/byte budget on `VaultSettings`, actuated at trash time** (pure function of bin contents, so replay is deterministic) | Bounded bin; each emitted purge carries its own journaled `authored_at` | **Verified precedent warning: `VaultSettings.retention` is plumbed end-to-end and never actuated.** Its only non-test read repo-wide is the encode arm at `settings.rs:925`; `Op::prune` (`op.rs:419-430`) has zero production callers; there is no `Command::Prune` (`facade.rs:807` is the unrelated `PruneInviteLinks`). `plan_prune` is called only from `publish_prune` (`drain.rs:1779`), which no production op reaches. A bin budget added the same way is the second dead setting — it ships with its actuation or not at all |
| **Time-based auto-purge via the clock seam** | What #1399's AC asks for; what v1 did (`recycleBinRetentionDays`, default 30, `v1:packages/core/src/vault/types.ts:73-84`) | v1's was an **opportunistic sweep on bin load** (`v1:apps/web/src/hooks/useBin.ts:45-52`) — if the user never opened the bin, nothing ever expired. Retention was advisory, not enforced. A clock branch inside a replayed decision makes two devices reach different bins, and it destroys data with no undo, hardest on the device offline longest — exactly the rule #1094 declined |

### D4 — Reclamation, and how purge settles (composes #1434 and #1094)

Purge is not "the bin's hard-delete path" — **purge is the reclamation the engine does not have at all**, bin or no bin (F1). `publish_prune` (`drain.rs:1751-1845`) is the template: it owes every doomed root to the `RetireLedger` (`drain.rs:1806-1809`, `seams/retire_ledger.rs:14-30`/`:69-80`) **before** publishing (`:1810-1839`), and refuses the whole op if a doomed CID is also named by a survivor (`drain.rs:1786-1801`).

**Refcounted unpin needs no new counter** — the safety property #1399's AC asks for is already implemented and tested: a target the live record still names retires nothing (`net/retire.rs:318-321`, test `:845-854`); a pass that cannot establish the live set stands down (`net/retire.rs:310-313`, test `:858-871`); register and retire derive their CID sets through one function with an equality invariant (`content/retention.rs:188-200`, test `:499-525`). Cross-*node* sharing is the registry's job (`CONTEXT.md:78` union liveness).

**The settlement hazard is real and confirmed with a sharper mechanism than the proposal stated.** `live_node_cids` (`drain.rs:1920-1942`) resolves the owing node by its *own derived write name* (`drain.rs:1925`) with `ResolveMode::NoCache`; a `None` skips the entry (`net/retire.rs:310-313`) and the ledger is never-discard by contract (`seams/retire_ledger.rs:62-65` — "There is no attempt budget, no expiry, and no sweep"). A plain `Delete` does *not* strand debt today, precisely because the record is never retired and keeps resolving. **Any purge that removes the record produces a permanently unsettleable debt: pinned bytes charged forever.**

| Option | Pro | Con |
|---|---|---|
| **New `OwedRetire` "no live record by construction" class** the pass treats as an empty live set | Cheapest; keeps the deliberate leak-not-loss polarity (`drain.rs:1918-1919`, `blueprint/engine.md:145-146`) | A new trust-shaped class in the ledger; needs its own test that a mislabeled entry cannot unpin a live record |
| **Retire the `ipnsName` only after content debt settles** | No ledger change | Leaves a resolvable record for an item the user was told is gone |
| **Never retire the name** (status quo) | Zero work | The #1434 leak stands: quota spent forever, republisher effort forever, and the F1 revocation hole stands |

**#1094 composes cleanly, not awkwardly:** a purge owes every version root through `version_cids` — the same channel `plan_prune` uses — so keep-latest-N and bin purge feed one ledger with no interaction beyond it. Note also that v2's location-independent node seeds delete an entire v1 problem class: v1 had to stash `originalFolderKeyEncrypted` on every bin entry and re-encrypt the record on restore (`v1:packages/core/src/bin/types.ts:60-72`); under D1-A there is nothing to re-encrypt.

### D5 — Command shape and the rebase rule (this is the one the proposal misses)

| Option | Pro | Con |
|---|---|---|
| **Repoint `Delete` at trash; `Purge` is the hard delete** | Every existing caller becomes recoverable by default, FUSE `unlink` included (`blueprint/desktop.md:192`); `delete` already has a wasm builder (`crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:991`) whereas **`Command::Move` has none** — so trash must reach web through `delete` regardless | Swaps the conditional-delete rebase rule for the Move rule (F2), amending `blueprint/engine.md:400` and contradicting `desktop.md:199`. Hits F3 — the FUSE junk sweep fills the bin |
| **Repoint `Delete`, but keep it rebasing under the *delete* rule** (relink mechanics, delete semantics: a concurrent edit drops the trash and the node stays put) | Preserves both blueprint rules unamended; the user-visible outcome ("edit wins") is identical to today | A relink that rebases like a delete is a new hybrid — needs its own rebase arm and tests. Still needs an F3 carve-out: an explicit hard-delete path for the junk sweep |
| **New `Trash` command; `Delete` unchanged** | No rebase-rule question at all | FUSE `unlink` stays a permanent delete unless separately rewired, so desktop deletes are unrecoverable — against `desktop.md:192` |

### D6 — What #1400 actually needs from the engine

Not a design choice so much as a cost the plan must carry. `snapshot()` refuses non-folders (`facade.rs:5634-5637`) and listing is strictly parent-keyed (`Snapshot::children`, `sync/model.rs:266-281`) — there is no predicate, no flat scan. The only flat facade read is `received_shares()` (`facade.rs:5690`), landed three days ago in `3d3ac0fc1`, which is the precedent to copy.

- **A new command** is a mechanical 5-file change: `facade.rs` (enum `:610` + `Debug` label `:794` + handler `:3663`) → `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs` builder → `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts:213` union → `commandCodec.ts:233` case (a missing case is a compile error via the `descriptor: never` bound at `:224-226`) → `packages/client/src/facade.ts` one-liner.
- **A new flat read is ~9 files**, because reads bypass the command envelope and every transport implements them individually (`engineHost` → `serve` → `transport` → `correlatedTransport` → `broadcast` → `broadcastTransport` → `leaderRelay` → `engineClient` → `facade`, plus `testkit`). Budget the read as the dominant client cost.
- Web side: `/bin` currently falls through the `*` catch-all (`apps/web/src/App.tsx:10-23`); `AppSidebar.tsx:13` is the `comingSoon` stub, `NavItem.tsx:77-88` discards `to` entirely when stubbed, and the `bin` icon already exists. `apps/web/src/stores/sharing.store.ts` is the right store shape (a projection with no independent writers); `useVaultActions.ts:1-6` states the law the page must obey — "the UI never patches its own listing," so a restore must re-read rather than optimistically remove the row.

---

## (c) Recommended package

1. **D1 → A, bin root per scope**, aggregated into one listing at the facade. The decisive reason is F1, and it is not the reason the proposal gave: only Option A keeps binned nodes inside the scope subtree, so they ride the lazy wave and a revocation actually cuts access to them. Options B and C leave a revoked grantee reading everything ever deleted. Accept the consequence: a scope's grantees see that scope's bin, and a grantee's delete lands in the shared bin (the only intra-scope option, and it matches "shared folder trash").
2. **D2 → the `ChildRef.origin` field.** Pay the one core wire change with real accept/reject vectors rather than smuggling a schema-less format through `unknown` or through the name string. This makes core gate engine, so slice core first.
3. **D5 → repoint `Delete`, keep the delete rebase rule** (option 2). It preserves `blueprint/engine.md:400` and `desktop.md:199` unamended, and it keeps `delete`'s existing wasm builder as the path to web — which matters, since `Command::Move` has no builder. Add an explicit hard-delete path for the FUSE junk sweep (`crates/fuse/src/ops.rs:1027-1046`) so `.DS_Store` never reaches the bin.
4. **D3 → no clock, no auto-purge in v2.0.** Purge is user-initiated, matching the standing rule at `blueprint/engine.md:796-797`. Display age from the journaled `deletedAt`; never branch on it. Surface bin bytes beside the quota rather than enforcing a budget — `pending_reclaim_bytes()` (`facade.rs:5614`) is the existing shape for exactly that kind of vault-level figure. Do not add a budget knob to `VaultSettings` unless its actuation ships in the same slice; `retention` is the cautionary precedent and it is verified dead. This requires amending #1399's own AC sketch, which currently asks for clock-driven expiry.
5. **D4 → land the reclamation first, separately, with the ledger class.** #1434 is a standing leak *and* a revocation hole on `main` today; it is landable on its own merits before any bin exists, and nothing about the bin should gate fixing it.

The package's coherence: every piece leans on machinery that already exists and is tested — intra-scope relink, the add/add auto-suffix comparator (`blueprint/engine.md:403`, not v1's `" (restored)"` scheme at `v1:packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:599-609`), the retire ledger's survivor check, union liveness at the registry. The only genuinely new primitives are a reserved node id, one optional wire field, and one ledger class.

Two v1 laws worth porting verbatim regardless of the picks: **fail-closed subtree enumeration** — an unenumerable descendant folder aborts the whole operation rather than half-reclaiming, with per-file CID capture staying best-effort (`v1:packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:219-234`, cycle-guard at `:244-247` against attacker-influenceable metadata) — and **restore's add-before-remove ordering**, so the item is listed at the destination while still recorded in the bin and is never lost mid-restore (`v1:packages/sdk/src/bin/index.ts:651-652`).

## (d) Size, and what it blocks

| Slice | Size | Files | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 — reclamation for the existing hard delete + the `OwedRetire` no-live-record class (**= #1434**) | M | `sync/drain.rs`, `net/retire.rs`, `sync/project.rs`, `seams/retire_ledger.rs` | none |
| S2 — core `ChildRef.origin` + accept/reject vectors + manifest counts + release-active encode check | S | `crates/core/src/seal/body.rs`, `kat/vectors/seal/*`, `kat/manifest.json` | none |
| S3 — bin root, reserved-id guard, trash, restore, `RestoreTargetGone`, bin filtering in `SnapshotView` | **L** | `facade.rs`, `sync/op.rs`, `sync/drain.rs`, `sync/project.rs`, `sync/model.rs`, `sync/rebase.rs`, `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs` | S2 |
| S4 — `Command::Purge` (accepted only under a bin root) + the bin-bytes report | M | `facade.rs`, `sync/drain.rs`, `net/retire.rs` | S1, S3 |
| S5 — wasm builders + TS codec + the flat bin read | M (the read dominates: 2 commands × 5 files + 1 read × 9 files) | `crates/wasm`, `packages/client` | S3, S4 |
| S6 — **#1400** `/bin` route, sidebar stub → live link, Playwright spec | M | `apps/web` | S5 |

Roughly 5-6 PRs; at the 2-3-issues-per-PR batching rule and the 1-review/hr CodeRabbit ceiling, that is two waves. Hot-file contention is the binding constraint as usual — `facade.rs` is 10,052 lines and `drain.rs` 3,648, and S3/S4/S5 all touch `facade.rs`, so they serialize. Wave 14 has no other engine slice open (#1370-#1400 are web/desktop/ci/deploy), so the hot files are free right now.

**Blocks:** #1400 (`blocked_by: #1399` today; its real edge is S5). **Unblocked by nothing** — S1 and S2 both have `blocked_by: none` and can start immediately in parallel. **Independent of #1094**, which shares only the retire ledger. Landing S1 alone closes #1434, recovers quota, stops the republisher re-PUTting unreachable records, and closes the F1 revocation residual — worth doing whichever way D1 goes.</result>
